requiredFindings.title: Four maxItems passages are JSON numbers and cannot bind
requiredFindings.problem: The first four passageOverrides select JSON numbers. The pinned checker returns that number and requires before and after to be strings equal to the selected value. The strings "1024" and "128" are not equal to the integers 1024 and 128, so binding fails with passage override before text differs from accepted parent. A line selector is also unavailable: v4 rejects line selectors on a JSON parent.
evidence: Product worktree /Users/sb/code/opensip-ai/opensip-fx-design at f5f5b4d20eca34ab2312b3ffc141c378da326afe, tools/verify_design.py sha256 7b313de629f2c958a1e62538b909d6f01545be2519238ba9b3d86ab7e7ba3326. selected_passage returns the decoded JSON value. contract_successor lines 248-251 require a string before and compare it with !=. Lines 401-408 raise v4 JSON parent passages require JSON Pointer selectors when a line selector's parent parses as JSON.

Executed that selected_passage on the six parent files. Overrides 0-3 return int and compare false: requestedCapabilities 1024, nativeContextDigests 128, and both notices 1024. Overrides 4-10, the seven prose lines, compare true.
The three candidate schema copies do contain the intended integers: requestedCapabilities 11264, nativeContextDigests 1024, both notices 11264. Those bytes are not what the passage check compares.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Delete the four numeric JSON-pointer overrides. Do not change verify_design in this unit. Keep those integers in the three candidate schema copies. Record the notice change as the string passage in FX-CAP-1-RF-02. The two identity maxima remain authorized by the majorLaw supersession, whose before already equals HSR-1's after and whose after names both identity increases. Do not replace the deleted numeric overrides with another pointer whose selected value is not text.

requiredFindings.title: Step notice description still states the retired 1024 bound
requiredFindings.problem: Both supplied common-schema copies, which the contract calls the implementation input, still say in the present tense that notices is bounded at 1024 because that is the analysis-spec requestedCapabilities bound, so a step collection can never truncate and noticeCount equals its array length. The same definition's maxItems is 11264, and this successor also changes the analysis-spec bound to 11264. The description and the keyword disagree. Native lines 1115, 1117 and 1119 and workflows line 1317 were updated; this description was not.
evidence: Independent deep diff: each workflow candidate differs from its parent by exactly notices.maxItems 1024 to 11264. CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1.description is unchanged in both copies and is the parent sentence at line 1499.

CONTRACT.md states that notices.maxItems becomes 11264 in both workflow common schema versions, preserving one notice per selected row without truncation, and that the exact schema copy is the implementation input.

The separate CapabilityAvailabilityV1 description, which begins 'An earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024', is historical and is not this finding. Native lines 1122-1123 and workflows lines 1318-1319, the 1023/2046 flat-array illustration, are also historical.
requiredFindings.requestedChange: Add a passage override of /$defs/CapabilityAvailabilityStepV1/description on each common-schema parent. before is that parent description exactly. after states the current bound and its reason as 11264, keeps one absence per requested row, keeps noticeCount equal to the array length, and keeps uniqueness within a step. Leave the historical flat-array sentence intact. Materialize both schema copies so the description matches and notices.maxItems remains the integer 11264. This string override is the bindable replacement for the two numeric notice overrides deleted under FX-CAP-1-RF-01.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The invocation description says an earlier revision used one flat array bounded at 1024, then continues 'but 1024 is per analysis-spec'. That sentence records the retired flat array. It is not the current per-step maximum. The same historical 1023/2046 illustration remains at native-evidence.md lines 1122-1123 and workflows-and-surfaces.md lines 1318-1319. CapabilityAvailabilityNoticeV1 still says BoundedText is 1024, which is the text-length bound, not the notice count.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Leave those historical sentences in this respin. A later wording pass may recast '1024 is per analysis-spec' as the earlier revision's bound.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The selected enumeration-plan description still says maxItems 128 is this array's bound, not plan.nativeContextDigests maxItems 128. This successor makes the Plan maximum 1024. The enumeration array's own maximum stays 128. The document is one of the eight payload-registry documents, and this subject correctly does not change it.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Correct that cross-reference in a later description revision that can carry the historical-reader row. Do not fold that byte change into FX-CAP-1.
